title: Site-wide client-side search for seeded updates

requirements.summary: Add a /search route page that filters seeded updates and renders results using the existing UpdateCard layout with SEO metadata.
acceptanceCriteria: A new route exists (e.g., /search) and renders inside the existing SiteLayout.
The Search page includes a search input with a clear label/placeholder in English (e.g., "Search updates...").
Typing a query filters across all available updates from the existing seed data (at minimum: title + excerpt; body matching is optional but if implemented must not break performance).
Results are shown as a responsive grid/list of existing UpdateCard components, and clicking a card navigates to the existing /post/$postId detail page.
When the query is empty, the page shows a helpful empty state (e.g., instructions or popular/latest items) instead of a blank list.
When there are zero matches, the page shows a clear “No results found” state with a suggestion to try different keywords.
The page sets appropriate SEO title and meta description via the existing usePageMeta hook.

file_operations.description: Create a Search page that renders inside the existing SiteLayout, sets SEO via usePageMeta, reads the initial query from the URL (q=...), provides a labeled input (e.g., "Search updates..."), and shows: (1) helpful empty state when query is empty (e.g., instructions + latest updates), (2) responsive UpdateCard grid/list for matches, (3) clear “No results found” state when there are zero matches. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.
Register a new /search route that renders SearchPage under the existing root route (SiteLayout), ensuring it is navigable and not orphaned.

Verify UpdateCard works seamlessly when rendered in a dense results grid/list (e.g., click target and spacing); if needed, make only non-breaking adjustments outside of frontend/src/components/ui to keep behavior consistent with /post/$postId navigation.

requirements.summary: Add desktop and mobile header search entry points that navigate to /search and prefill the query via the URL parameter (q).
acceptanceCriteria: Desktop header provides a visible search control (input or button) without overcrowding the existing navigation links.
Mobile navigation provides a search entry point that is easy to tap and does not reduce menu usability (menu remains scrollable).
Submitting a search from header/mobile navigates to the Search page and includes the query in the URL (e.g., q=term).
The Search page reads the URL query parameter on load and shows the corresponding filtered results.
The search UI is mobile-safe (no overlaps, input/button fits on small screens, appropriate spacing).

file_operations.description: Add a lightweight desktop header search control (small input or input+icon button) that submits to /search with q=... without overcrowding existing nav links; ensure spacing and responsive behavior remain intact.

Add a mobile search entry point within the existing Sheet menu (e.g., a search input at the top or a dedicated Search link/button) that is easy to tap, keeps the menu scrollable, and navigates to /search with q=... when submitted.
Ensure the Search page reads q from the URL on initial load and updates its input/results accordingly; optionally keep URL q in sync when the user submits/commits a new query from within the page.

requirements.summary: Implement fast, deterministic, dependency-light client-side string matching for searching seeded updates.
acceptanceCriteria: Search implementation uses simple string matching and does not introduce heavy third-party search libraries.
Search is case-insensitive and trims extra whitespace in the query.
Search results order is deterministic (e.g., newest first among matches or stable original order) and does not flicker between renders.
No backend changes are required for search; search works offline against the existing seeded content model.

file_operations.description: Add lightweight search utilities for UpdateItem seeded content: normalize query (trim/collapse whitespace, lowercase), perform simple substring matching against at least title and excerpt (optionally body), and return deterministically ordered results (e.g., stable sort by date desc with tie-breaker by original index) to avoid render flicker.
Use the new client-side search utility to filter across all seeded updates; memoize derived lists to keep search fast for the current dataset and ensure deterministic ordering.
If needed for clean composition, export a minimal helper to retrieve all seeded updates (or a pre-sorted view) for search without duplicating logic across pages; keep it offline and dependency-free.
